steps.say: Most childhood myocarditis starts with an ordinary virus. Enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus B, adenovirus, parvovirus B19, and human herpesvirus 6 are the commonest identified triggers. The immune response that clears the virus then turns on the heart muscle, so cardiac symptoms typically follow the febrile illness by one to two weeks.
steps.tx: Common **viral pathogens** of paediatric myocarditis are **enteroviruses (coxsackievirus B)**, **adenovirus**, **parvovirus B19**, and **human herpesvirus 6**. Direct viral injury plus the ensuing immune attack on shared myocardial antigens produces the clinical picture, which is why new heart failure or arrhythmia within weeks of a viral illness should raise immediate suspicion.

steps.say: Blood tests confirm that heart muscle is dying. Cardiac troponin I and T rise in over 80 percent of children with acute myocarditis, making them sensitive markers of active cardiomyocyte necrosis. A raised troponin in a child with a recent viral illness and new cardiac signs should be treated as myocarditis until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: **Troponin elevation** marks active injury: cardiac **troponin I and T** are raised in over **80%** of children with acute myocarditis and serve as sensitive biomarkers of ongoing **cardiomyocyte necrosis**. Unlike adult infarction, the rise may be modest and prolonged, natriuretic peptides track the accompanying ventricular strain, and normal troponin never excludes the diagnosis alone.

points: Troponin raised in over 80% of cases
Modest prolonged rise typical of inflammation
left.title: Troponin in Myocarditis

points: Follows the degree of heart failure
Guides diuresis and follow up timing
right.title: Natriuretic Peptides

steps.say: Magnetic resonance now diagnoses myocarditis without a biopsy in most children. The updated Lake Louise criteria demand both myocardial edema on T2 mapping and non ischaemic injury on T1 mapping, extracellular volume, or late gadolinium enhancement. Meeting both arms confirms inflammation with accuracy that rivals tissue diagnosis.
steps.tx: The updated **Cardiac MRI Lake Louise Criteria** require **myocardial edema** shown by **T2 mapping** or raised T2 signal plus **non ischaemic myocardial injury** shown by **T1 mapping**, expanded **extracellular volume**, or subepicardial **late gadolinium enhancement**. Both arms must be positive, the injury must spare the subendocardium unlike infarction, and follow up scans track healing or scar.

vis.alt: Short axis cardiac MRI pairs T2 weighted oedema images with contrast images showing subepicardial enhancement sparing the subendocardium.
vis.caption: Lateral wall edema with non ischaemic outer wall injury of myocarditis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: When imaging leaves doubt, a tiny piece of heart muscle settles it. The Dallas criteria require an inflammatory cellular infiltrate invading the myocardium together with degeneration and necrosis of adjacent myocytes. Borderline cases without necrosis are reported as such, and immunostaining plus viral genome testing now sharpen the yield.
steps.tx: The histological **Dallas criteria** diagnose myocarditis on **endomyocardial biopsy** by requiring a myocardial **inflammatory cellular infiltrate** associated with **myocyte degeneration and necrosis** unrelated to ischaemia. Sampling error limits sensitivity since inflammation is patchy, so multiple samples with immunohistochemistry and viral polymerase chain reaction complete the modern biopsy assessment.

vis.alt: Microscopic view of lymphocytic myocardial infiltration with myocyte necrosis and interstitial edema.
vis.caption: Lymphocytic infiltrate with myocyte necrosis meeting Dallas criteria. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Calming the immune storm is as important as supporting the pump. High dose intravenous immunoglobulin at 2 grams per kilogram over 24 to 48 hours is widely used in acute paediatric myocarditis for its immunomodulatory effects. Corticosteroids are added to the regimen in fulminant or autoantibody positive cases under specialist guidance.
steps.tx: **Immunoglobulin therapy in myocarditis** uses high dose **intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)** at **2 g/kg** over **24-48 hours** for immunomodulatory effects in acute paediatric disease. Corticosteroids are added for fulminant presentations and virus negative inflammatory cardiomyopathy, while antiviral strategies remain investigational and routine immunosuppression is avoided with proven active viral genomes.

nodes.label: Acute myocarditis confirmed by troponin, MRI, or biopsy criteria
IVIG 2 g/kg over 24-48 hours modulates the immune attack
Steroids added for fulminant or virus negative inflammation
Pump support with milrinone or ECMO bridges recovery

steps.say: A failing inflamed ventricle needs support that unloads rather than squeezes blindly. Milrinone is preferred over pure alpha agonists because its inodilator action improves contractility while dilating vessels and cutting afterload. Excessive tachycardia is avoided since fast rates starve the inflamed myocardium of diastolic coronary filling.
steps.tx: **Inotropic support in fulminant myocarditis** favours **milrinone** over pure alpha agonists for its **inodilator properties** that reduce afterload while improving contractility without excessive tachycardia. Low dose adrenaline backs the circulation when hypotension persists, arrhythmia surveillance runs continuously, and mechanical ventilation unloads the failing ventricle by cutting work of breathing.

points: Vasodilation cutting afterload and wall stress
Little tachycardia, kinder to ischaemic muscle
left.title: Milrinone

points: Higher oxygen demand from fast heart rates
right.title: Pure Alpha Agonists

steps.say: Some hearts need complete rest to survive the storm. Venoarterial ECMO takes over pumping and oxygenation while the inflamed myocardium recovers, and survival to discharge exceeds 70 to 80 percent because the injury is often fully reversible. Early transfer to an ECMO centre saves lives when inotropes alone cannot hold the circulation.
steps.tx: **VA-ECMO support** provides crucial hemodynamic rescue for fulminant myocarditis, with **survival to discharge exceeding 70-80%** thanks to the potential for **complete myocardial recovery**. Cannulation unloads the heart fully, anticoagulation is balanced against bleeding, and transplantation rather than recovery becomes the goal only when serial imaging shows no return of function.

steps.say: Exercise too soon after myocarditis can kill. Complete cessation of competitive sports and vigorous activity for at least 3 to 6 months is mandatory, with return only after normal examination, biomarkers, imaging, and rhythm monitoring. The scarred or healing muscle remains electrically unstable long after the child feels well.
steps.tx: **Exercise restriction** mandates complete cessation of **competitive sports** and vigorous physical activity for at least **3 to 6 months** following acute myocarditis. Clearance needs normalised troponin and natriuretic peptides, resolved MRI edema, preserved ejection fraction, and no exercise induced arrhythmia, since exertion during healing risks sudden death from unstable scar.

nodes.label: Acute myocarditis diagnosed and sport stopped for 3 to 6 months
Biomarkers, MRI, echo, and rhythm strip all return to normal
Graded return to play follows cardiology clearance only
